I am 61 years old. I never went to school. I have farmed for 40 years, and I learned everything by watching and doing. My family has 13.1 mu of land. I put 10 mu into wheat and maize, one after the other, and I keep 3.1 mu for cotton. My son and daughter-in-law work in the city, but they send money. Still, I count every yuan.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the dealer — the same kind my neighbor Old Wang used. Before October sowing, I have the tractor man rotary-till the 10 mu. I spread one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer on each mu as base. In spring, when the wheat turns green, I broadcast 25 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: winter water, jointing water, and one more when the grain is filling. I spray twice for weeds and bugs. I hire three people for two days to help harvest in June. I expect about 450 kilograms per mu.

For maize, right after the wheat comes off in June, I plant hybrid maize seed on the same 10 mu. I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows at sowing. When the plants are knee-high, I side-dress 25 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once after sowing if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. Two sprays. I expect about 550 kilograms per mu.

For cotton, I plough the 3.1 mu deep because cotton likes loose soil. I plant hybrid cotton in April. I put one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. At flowering, I spread 25 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate three times and spray three times for insects. Last year I tried to save on spray and the worms ate the bolls, so I will not cut back. I hire local women to help pick in autumn. I expect about 280 kilograms of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive, but a bad harvest is worse than wasting a little fertilizer. I watch my neighbors. If they put more, I put more. If they irrigate, I irrigate.
